newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines says to save money on yankee issue.
newsitem.headline: Philippines says to save money on yankee issue.

text.p: The Philippine Central Bank said on Tuesday it would save money on its revamped yankee bond issue and hoped to have its side of the deal wrapped up by the end of the month.
Governor Gabriel Singson confirmed that Salomon Brothers had been named the firm underwriter out of five banks bidding for the position.
Six banks were originally involved in the issue, postponed in April because the rates were too high, but Singson would not identify which bank had dropped out.
"We're extremely pleased with the results," he told reporters.
"This a vindication of the decision to postpone the launch... it's a very good spread for us," he said.
Singson declined to give any details of the bond which in April was expected to be priced at a spread of around 225 basis points over U.S. Treasuries, too high for Manila which pulled the deal.
But because the U.S. long bond yield has fallen and because also a tighter spread, the Philippines would save $5 million a year for the next 30 years,' he added, but did not elaborate.
"It was not difficult for us to make a decision," he said when asked if the bids were competitive.
Under the deal, Salomon Brothers will underwrite the whole issue and pay the Philippines the proceeds direct. It is up to Salomon Brothers to decide on when to issue the bond.
"I would expect everything (the payment to the Philippines) to be done before the end of the month."
Singson dismissed as largely untrue reports of squabbling among the original group of underwriters -- Salomon Brothers, Citibank NA, Morgan Stanley, Merrill Lynch, JP Morgan and ING Barings.
"Many of them (the reports) are not true ... the bidders are convinced about fairness and transparency of the bidding," he added.
Bids closed on Tuesday morning for the issue of 30- and 100-year bonds which the Philippines has said would be scaled down to below $750 from an earlier planned $1 billion.
